accuracy.evidence: Checked against the PSHE Association Programme of Study (2020) Key Stage 2 Health and Wellbeing outcomes on recognising individuality and personal qualities, identifying strengths, skills and achievements, and managing setbacks by re-framing unhelpful thinking, and CASEL's self-awareness competence (having a growth mindset). The adult text states the mindset evidence honestly: the message works best paired with effective strategies and support (Sisk et al. 2018, Yeager and Dweck 2020), and it names maturation as a real cause of change, so nothing claims all growth is effort.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: believing hard things stay hard (timeline prediction, fractions challenge), thinking skilled people were born that way (cause prediction, cartwheel challenge), crediting effort for every change (Rosa's shelf, Ali's bar), comparing with the strongest peer (Mo's lap time, drawing item), reading one dip as no progress (Jas's line graph, Tom's scores 4, 6, 5, 8), and trusting feelings or praise over a record of work (Sam's pages).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagthennow is built on looking back across time: a three-slot Age 6, Age 8, Now timeline filled in order, a four-way cause sort (practice, help, new strategy, growing up) with a different wrong-answer reason for every cause in every story, a Fixed versus Growth drop zone, and evidence views drawn for the round (lap-time bars, a progress line with a dip, page stacks). Highest 6-token overlap with any other flagship lab is 9% (flag_pgnext, shared shell code).

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers before being told: tapping Reads chapter books alone first says it shows more skill so comes later, which shows change came in steps; choosing Practice for Leo says his sister holding the seat is help; choosing Practice for Rosa says you cannot practise being taller; choosing Her growth has stopped points to the whole line on the graph. Each done message states the rule after the task.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: always be hard for you (three timelines show earlier hard skills became easy), born good at it (all four stories have a named cause), and adding yet changes nothing (the sort shows yet sentences are the ones that leave room to change). The done message reports the prediction back.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with shuffled options and a separate message for every wrong option, e.g. one drop from 6 to 5 is a dip, from 4 to 8 overall he has improved; you cannot practise being taller; comparing with friends tells you nothing about your own change; one comment is not a record of change. Wrong lab choices also name the slip for that story.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation scores Flesch-Kincaid grade 3.2 and the adult text 7.8, inside the learner limits of 6.5 and 9.5. Canvas sentences are short; terms are defined where used (fixed thinking says I can never change, growth thinking says not yet or I have improved; a strategy is a new way of doing it).

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a cause type, a fair-comparison rule, a named mistake or an evidence example. The explanation is under 1% the same as any other lesson (nearest: Community Rights and Responsibilities and Persisting When It's Hard), and there is no be-positive padding: the growth claim is grounded in the learner's own past.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots of every step in dark and light: the three timeline slots fit side by side with 13 px card text, the four cause tiles sit in a 2 by 2 grid, the Fixed and Growth boxes fit side by side under the sentence card, and the lap-time bars, dip graph and page stacks fit above full-width answer cards. Every control has a button twin below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: all four tasks finish with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, and axe-core finds no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme, with no console errors. Every drag has a labelled button twin (e.g. Put Knew some letter sounds in the next slot; I am just bad at drawing is fixed thinking), and each result is spoken via the live region and the canvas aria-label.

sources: PSHE Association (2020) Programme of Study for PSHE Education, Key Stage 2 Health and Wellbeing: self-concept (individuality, strengths, skills and achievements; managing setbacks and re-framing unhelpful thinking)
CASEL (2020) SEL Framework: self-awareness, including having a growth mindset
Yeager, D. S. and Dweck, C. S. (2020) What can be learned from growth mindset controversies? American Psychologist 75(9)
Sisk, V. F. et al. (2018) To what extent and under which circumstances are growth mind-sets important to academic achievement? Psychological Science 29(4)
